div.head: Wi 1.1
div.ab: ⁊ man for cyning gebidde, ⁊ hine buton neadhæse heora willum weorþigen.
⁊ man for cyning gebidde, ⁊ hine buton neadhæse heora willum weorþigen.
⁊ man for cyning gebidde ⁊ hine buton neadhæse heora willum weorþigen
und man bete für den König, und sie mögen ihn ohne Zwangsgeheiss aus ihrem [freien] Willen verehren.
and one is to pray for the king, and they are to honour him of their [free] will without compulsion.
The king shall be prayed for, and they shall honour him freely and without compulsion.
And the king is to be prayed for, and they are to honour him of their own free-will without compulsion.
and one should pray for the king, and do him honor of their own will without compulsion.

note.seg: Stubbs Constit. hist. I 175 verbindet richtig diesen Satz mit dem vorigen: ‘intercession for the king shall be part of the ordinary service of the church’; s. Gl Fürbitte 2ff.; Kirchenstaatsrecht 4a ff.

Stubbs Constit. hist. I 175 rightly connects this clause with the preceding one: ‘intercession for the king shall be part of the ordinary service of the church’; see Gl Fürbitte 2ff.; Kirchenstaatsrecht 4a ff.
‘injunction, a command attended by compulsion’ Toller. Das Kompositum scheint sonst nicht belegt
‘injunction, a command attended by compulsion’ Toller. The compound appears not to be attested elsewhere
Die Freiwilligkeit bezieht sich nicht bloss auf die Fürbitte; sondern gemeint ist wohl: Klerus trete allgemein beim Volke fürs Königtum in Predigt, Ermahnung, Beispiel ein

The voluntariness does not refer merely to the intercession; rather, what is meant is probably that the clergy should in general champion the kingship among the people by preaching, exhortation and example
